editorial:
Imagine being hated by your own family and kicked out of your home just because people think you support the enemy. That is exactly where you find Sally Maitland, and she is stuck on a ship to Canada with a bunch of strangers. You get to meet two very different men: a charming Polish prince and a shy British spy. The whole trip feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where nobody is telling the truth. It is a slow-burn mystery that keeps you wondering who is actually a double agent and who is just trying to survive the war.

What really makes this one work is how it keeps you guessing about the characters' real identities. The acting is solid for the time, though some of the dialogue feels a bit stiff. If you love old-school spy stories with lots of secrets, you will really dig this. It might feel a bit slow in the middle, but the payoff is worth it. Since it is an older film, you should try to find a restored version.
endingExplained: You find out that Jan Orloch is actually a Nazi spy and not a Polish prince at all. He was using Sally to get secret information. In the end, Jimmy Garrick reveals he is a clever intelligence officer who was onto Jan the whole time. After a tense showdown, the spy is caught and stopped. Sally finally clears her name and finds true love with Jimmy, proving she was never a traitor.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old spy movies and wartime mysteries.
